title: Emergence — Target
description: What cfr-creator pulls the physics field toward. Optional on every tick() call -- omit it and the field runs untargeted, claiming no convergence. If omitted mid-session, the previous tick's target is reused (the real feedback mechanism -- see loop.js). Matches cfr-creator/component.spec and cfr-creator/index.js exactly.

id.description: By convention, prefixed with the type: 'end-state:repair-complete', 'idea:a1b2c3', 'person:raven'. Not enforced by code -- a convention, not a constraint. If it's a real idea, use idea-store's real id (idea-store/index.js's add() return value).

type.description: What kind of thing this target represents. Purely descriptive -- cfr-creator treats all three identically (gravitational attractor). The distinction exists for your own reasoning about what you're pursuing, not for different physics.

mass.description: How strongly the field is pulled toward this target. Empirically characterized (not guessed): mass=3 converges unreliably within a reasonable tick budget (physics.js's field.curl genuinely competes with gravity at range -- checked DEFAULT_CONFIG). mass=15 converges reliably within ~60 ticks. See cfr-creator/component.spec's known_gap for the full empirical basis.
